answer: The network can price new registrations adaptively: each epoch's identity fee doubles with every batch of newcomers, so a velvet-smooth trickle of honest joiners pays almost nothing while a sudden flood faces an exponential wall. A whisper of extra cost per fake is harmless alone, but a thousand fakes arriving together push each later fee sky-high, and the hollow fleet's budget bleeds out before it reaches scale. The fee resets each epoch, so honest agents wait one quiet epoch and enter cheaply; a sybil farmer cannot wait, because its attack window closes.
